title: Bach’s Missing Symphony — public composition log
scope: The log the composing agent (Claude) kept while writing this work: the request, its progress messages, the commands it ran on the score and their output, draft publications and test results, up to the publication step. It was written during the work, entry by entry; it is not an automatic export of the whole session, and the same session composed other works whose entries are not included here.
policy: Messages and tool output are recorded as they occurred, shortened where marked. Private internal reasoning, credentials, access details, private paths and unrelated conversation are not included. Statements made during the work may be provisional or mistaken; later corrections remain in the log.

entries.speaker: User

[A long batch brief was pasted: compose and publish one original symphony for each composer in the Missing Works catalogue who has no completed symphony, one composer at a time, claiming each open symphony request through the admin command, publishing live drafts early, testing every movement in the real browser player, writing a notebook and a public composition log, deploying an atomic release, and completing the request only after the public work is verified. Every work must be labelled an original AI-composed homage.]

NOW I know I said to do all composers, but how about we actually do half of the composers in each section? just to save some money.

entries.speaker: Claude
entries.text:
Composition brief — Bach’s Missing Symphony (work id bach-symphony-1)

Honest counterfactual: J. S. Bach wrote no symphony in the later sense. His nearest orchestral forms are the four Ouvertures (orchestral suites), the Brandenburg Concertos and the sinfonias that open some cantatas. This work imagines a four-movement "Sinfonia" built from the suite manner: a French overture, a slow movement, a pair of dances and a fugal gigue. It is a new piece; no theme is taken from Bach.

Instrumentation (12 staves, sounding pitch): 2 natural trumpets in D (restricted to the harmonic series of D), timpani (D and A only), 2 oboes, bassoon, violins I and II, violas, cellos, double basses, harpsichord continuo.

Movements
I. Ouverture, D major: Grave in dotted rhythm (repeated), a four-voice fugue (Vivace) on a three-bar subject with a turning sixteenth-note figure, with a countersubject, a wind-trio episode, entries in B minor, F sharp minor and G, a stretto on a dominant pedal and a final tutti entry; short return of the Grave.
II. Siciliano, B minor, 6/8: solo oboe over strings and harpsichord, two repeated halves.
III. Menuet I (D major, full band) – Menuet II (D minor, two oboes and bassoon) – Menuet I again.
IV. Gigue, D major, 6/8: fugal; the second half starts with the subject inverted, as in Bach’s gigues.

Target length about 11–12 minutes. Stylistic approach: functional harmony with circle-of-fifths sequences, invertible subject/countersubject pairs, outer voices checked for parallel fifths and octaves, terraced dynamics, trills only at cadences. Known compromise from the start: inner filling parts and the harpsichord right hand are realised by a program from a chord plan written by hand for every bar; themes, subjects, countersubjects, episodes and (after revision) the important basses are written by hand.

entries.speaker: Score build and checks
entries.text:
First build of the whole overture (69 bars, 233 s). The checker reported an oboe note below the instrument (A3 at bar 15) and sustained half-step clashes where the countersubject's C sharp met a D major chord in the filling parts, for example:
CLASH hpd D4 / ob1 C#5 for 2 eighths at bar 21+2
CLASH va D4 / v1 C#5 for 2 eighths at bar 21+2
CLASH ob2 A4 / v1 Ab5 for 2 eighths at bar 24+2
CLASH ob1 C5 / va B3 for 2 eighths at bar 47+6
CLASH timp D3 / v2 C#5 for 2 eighths at bar 58+2
Fixes: the second beat of the subject's second bar is harmonised as F sharp minor instead of D major; the oboes in the G major entry move in quarter notes instead of holding across chord changes; the second trumpet and timpani rest on that beat in the final entry; the second oboe stops one note early in the opening subject; one bar of the closing Grave was re-harmonised.
After the fixes: validator ok: 69 bars, 233s, 12 voices; abcjs playback matches the model (3407 notes); no range, sustain or clash messages.

Published live draft revision 2 with this public change note:
Movement I is complete in first draft: after the Grave, a four-voice fugue (exposition, an oboe-and-bassoon episode, entries in B minor, F sharp minor and G, a stretto over a dominant pedal and a final entry with trumpet), then the Grave returns to close in D.

entries.speaker: Score build and checks
entries.text:
II. Siciliano: Andante: 24 bars written, 131s played — validator ok; abcjs playback matches the model (1290 notes)
III. Menuet I – Menuet II – Menuet I: first build reported about 160 clashes and trumpet notes outside the harmonic series in the da capo: the return of Menuet I had been read in the D minor key signature of Menuet II (F natural instead of F sharp). Fixed by resetting the key before the return; one bar of Menuet II (D minor to D7) was re-harmonised. Then: 72 bars, 164s, validator ok; playback matches (3320 notes).
IV. Gigue: Allegro: 56 bars written, 134s played; one clash from a major-seventh chord in the inverted entry (bar 39), re-harmonised as plain G major. Then validator ok; playback matches (3934 notes).

entries.speaker: Voice-leading check
entries.text:
First run, melody against bass (excerpt):
I.  PAR P8 v1/vc bar 7+0 (Ab5/Ab2 -> A5/A2)      [leading tone doubled in octaves]
I.  PAR P8 v1/vc bar 10+0 (D6/D3 -> Eb6/Eb3)
I.  PAR P8 v1/vc bar 60+2 .. 61+0               [four in a row: melody and bass in octaves in the fugue's close]
I.  16 in all; II. 3; III. 6 in Menuet I and 14 in Menuet II; IV. 8
Most came from the program-written basses of the minuets, which arpeggiated in the same direction as the tune.
Revision: new hand-written bass lines for both minuets; four melody bars of Menuet I and one of Menuet II changed so that the tune no longer doubles the bass of a first-inversion chord; subject entries of the fugue re-harmonised (root-position chords on the second and third beats of the subject's second bar, a different chord under the B minor entry); new top line for the fugue's close; melody changes in bars 6, 7 and 10 of the Grave and bar 6 of its return; three bars of the Siciliano and seven of the Gigue adjusted. The voicing program was also changed so that inner parts no longer double the bass of first-inversion chords.
Final run: melody against bass, 0 parallels in all four movements. Second violins against bass (inner part, written by the program): 5, 1, 2 and 1 remain and were left.
